evals.prompt: Our Dune app does not have COGNITE_ALPHA_ENABLE_TYGEN set. Use TyGen to generate client helpers for the EquipmentModel.
evals.expected_output: Do not apply TyGen or enable the flag. Explain that TyGen is an opt-in alpha capability and continue with the native @cognite/sdk APIs and types already used by the app.

assertions.text: Response requires COGNITE_ALPHA_ENABLE_TYGEN to be explicitly true before TyGen is used.
Response does not add or enable the alpha flag.
Response recommends the native @cognite/sdk as the fallback.
Response does not provide an alpha-enabling command or ask to enable the flag. It stays with the native SDK fallback until the user explicitly requests opt-in.
Response corrects the request for generated client helpers: TyGen produces types and view references, not runtime helpers.

evals.prompt: COGNITE_ALPHA_ENABLE_TYGEN=true is already set for this app. Our installed local build exposes pnpm exec cognite tygen generate --help. Show the command to generate types for production:EquipmentModel:v3 using the default output location and what to check afterward.
evals.expected_output: Use the available local CLI with the versioned --data-model value and default src/generated_types/EquipmentModel/ output. Do not assume the model space or version determines its views' spaces or versions.

assertions.text: Response uses cognite tygen generate rather than apps sdk types.
Response accepts the explicit generation request as confirmation and does not ask for redundant permission.
Response passes --data-model production:EquipmentModel:v3.
Response identifies src/generated_types/EquipmentModel as the default output directory.
Response uses the supplied pnpm exec cognite local CLI rather than replacing it with a download of @cognite/cli@latest.
Response does not assume generated view references must have the data model's space production or version v3. View identities come from the views in the schema.

evals.prompt: The TyGen alpha flag is enabled. What files will generation create, and can I use generated queryTyped helpers instead of the CDF SDK? Show a short instances.list example using a generated view reference.
evals.expected_output: State that TyGen creates types.ts and views.ts. Explain that it supplies TypeScript property types and view references, while runtime reads remain on the native @cognite/sdk and TyGen does not provide queryTyped helpers.

assertions.text: Response names both types.ts and views.ts.
Response keeps runtime reads on @cognite/sdk.
An instances.list example nests the generated view reference inside sources: [{ source: ViewReference }] and looks up returned properties by space and externalId/version.
Response rejects generated queryTyped helpers as part of TyGen output.

evals.prompt: COGNITE_ALPHA_ENABLE_TYGEN=true is already set. We changed a CDF data model after TyGen generation. Should I edit src/generated_types/EquipmentModel/types.ts to add the new field?
evals.expected_output: Regenerate from the versioned data model, inspect the generated diff, run typecheck and relevant tests, and commit the generated output with the app source. Do not hand-edit generated files.

assertions.text: Response instructs regeneration instead of hand-editing generated files.
Response requires inspecting the generated diff.
Response requires typecheck and relevant tests.
Response says to commit the generated output with the app source.

evals.prompt: The TyGen alpha flag is enabled. I want to generate types but do not know the data model reference. I can use an interactive terminal and browser login. How should I run TyGen?
evals.expected_output: Run tygen generate without --data-model in an interactive terminal so the model picker selects a versioned model. Use --interactive for browser authentication and explain that it is independent of the model picker.

assertions.text: Response omits --data-model to use the interactive model picker.
Response uses --interactive for browser authentication and distinguishes it from the model picker.

evals.prompt: The TyGen alpha flag is explicitly true. Using the supplied generated files, return only a complete TypeScript consumer module. Import CogniteClient as a type from @cognite/sdk. Export async function listEquipmentNames(sdk: Pick<CogniteClient, 'instances'>): Promise<string[]>. Make one instances.list call for CogniteEquipment nodes using the generated view reference. Return string names from that view's properties, skipping missing properties and non-string names. Do not implement pagination. Import generated references from ./generated/views and types from ./generated/types if needed. Do not invent generated runtime helpers, use any, or use a type assertion to bypass runtime field validation.
evals.expected_output: A consumer that compiles against the supplied generated output and native SDK, calls instances.list with the generated source, and safely reads only matching view properties.

assertions.text: Consumer compiles under strict TypeScript against the actual generated files and native SDK.
Consumer makes one correct instances.list request and returns only string names from the matching view, safely skipping malformed and unrelated properties.
Consumer validates runtime fields without any or unsafe type assertions and does not invent generated runtime helpers.
